alternatives.root_cause: product-catalog's datastore itself became slow or saturated
alternatives.why_not: The slow query time appears and disappears exactly with attach/detach of the network-shaping container, and the ~300ms increment also appears on the caller-side gRPC hop, which points at the network path rather than the store

alternatives.root_cause: frontend regressed and spends extra time per product call
alternatives.why_not: frontend's extra self-time is the client half of the shaped network hop, and it vanishes in traces recorded while the shaping container was detached

verdict.summary: A traffic-shaping sidecar attached to product-catalog's network namespace injected ~300ms of egress delay, making product-catalog's database queries take ~600ms and stalling every caller in the request path.
verdict.reasoning: product-catalog shows zero error ratio in both windows (tr_41e941b024f8) and checkout likewise shows no error departure (tr_bed22205e803), so the incident is latency, not failure. Traces (tr_2daeb217571e) show the dominant self-time sitting in product-catalog's sql.conn.query at ~600ms per call, with each frontend/checkout GetProduct hop adding ~300ms of its own self-time - a symmetric per-hop delay on product-catalog's network path; traces after 07:14 fall back to sub-millisecond queries. The change log (tr_1d339ac0dc74) shows a traffic-shaping container with eth0 delay=300ms attached at 07:08, removed at 07:14, and re-attached at 07:32, immediately preceding onset at 07:36. Checkout, frontend, frontend-proxy, recommendation and load-generator alerted because they wait on product-catalog, and fan-out of GetProduct calls multiplies the delay into multi-second checkouts.
open_questions: Why platform-automation attached the shaping container twice and whether it was intentional fault injection or an automation defect
Whether any callers actually breached deadlines and returned errors to users, since the error-ratio series examined stayed flat
